The best option, (and history bears this out: end of serfdom, end of slavery, etc.) is market with as thoroughly distributed market power as possible. That is, as close to "Perfect Competition" as possible. This is what people used to recognize as a "free market", but that term has become conflated with big business interests kept in power by government protections. That's not a free market of course, but a highly controlled one by select interests, and when this happens -- as in the case of monopoly or oligopoly for instance -- firms gather undue market power, they can fix prices and production, and the population suffers as a result. (This is similar to the issue with Communism: even a well-meaning central authority begins creating huge issues in production to meet demand. This down to the problem of "distributed knowledge" which highly distributed markets solve effectively.)

Want to save humanity? Think of how you can create a situation as close to perfect competition as possible, and to maintain it. This means firms can't set prices, and the actual needs of human beings are reflected in the market. Probably that would mean less government intervention on the side of economic stimulus, and more on the side of breaking up large corporations which have gathered undue market power.
